item.title: Comment on It’s happening at The New York Times by Blackthorne
item.description:
Reply to Der Zeit:

The Times as a news source was lost long ago to first contact with AI and the need to conform to the imperatives of the dopamine/attention economy. It’s 85% recipes and word games and lifestyle and coffee grinder reviews and identity and diet and exercise routines. The information density is LOW. Will generative AI change that? (Especially as it becomes ubiquitous?) Doubtful.

The information density is low perhaps if you read every single thing on the NYT website, but cooking/games/wirecutter aren't published at the expense of the higher information density articles. If anything these sections subsidize the higher information density articles. The fluff sections are also the sections where generative AI is likely to be more effective, so if anything it should free up resources for the journalistic arm of the NYT
